The short of it is I went with BUP. To hear how I integratted it with ssh read on.

What I wanted to do, and what I got done, was to make it back up every time I log in with ssh. This has the advantage that until I have a location I want to send it network accessable I can take advantage of a reverse tunnel through the ssh and bring it local. A random port needed to be used in the reverse tunnel so that if a shell hangs we don't have trouble binding to the port.

File dump, first a function declaration:

dev () 
{ 
 RPORT=`shuf -i 2000-65000 -n 1`
 echo $RPORT
 ssh -t -R $RPORT:localhost:22 xxDOMAINxx "
 echo $RPORT
 bin/autobupremote $RPORT
 bash"
}

RPORT is the port for the reverse proxy. We echo on both the client and server side to verify agreement. We tell it to run the update script and then we open a shell. The -t assigns a new virtual console to the session giving me a prompt and allowing things like htop and tmux to work. I will likely replace the call with bin/autobupremote $RPORT > /dev/null & possibly 2> /dev/null but likely not. For now it's good to see it's working.

Now the update script

#!/bin/bash

echo "
Host laptop
 HostName laptop
 Port "$1"
 User xxxUSERxxx
 StrictHostKeyChecking no
" > ~/.ssh/config

bup index src
bup save -r laptop:.bup -n src src

When using bup remotely we can't pass ssh paramaters so we have to do it in .ssh/config, and our port changes. laptop also needs to be defined in /etc/hosts with 127.0.0.1. Each time we connect to a new port ssh thinks it's a new host so a prompt appears and bup can't handle the prompt so we turn that off just for this applications. We know the tunnel is ours, we just set it up. We then make an index and send it to the remote.

Short commings: I wanted to set up the repository in a partition on my LVM set up for data instead of in /home but the bup web command only like to read from ~/.bup. I can symlink it I suppose but it would be nice if bup web could inspect different locations.

Strengths: I can control the frequency of backups. If I want highly granular backups I can just log out and in for each task I work on. If I want a day's work in each snapshot I just log into ssh each day and use tmux for each session. Bup, based on git, handles text files really well but also has alterations that makes it good at handling binary data, even frequently changing files like sqlite.
